mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about gases is a common misconception?

options.B: Gases expand to fill the shape of their container.
options.C: The particles of a gas are far apart from each other.

mcqs.explanation: Gases do NOT have a fixed shape; they take the shape of whatever container they are in. Options B, C and D correctly describe gases, while A is the misconception.

mcqs.question: Why can a gas flow from one place to another?

options.A: Because its particles are far apart and move freely in all directions.
options.B: Because it has a rigid, fixed structure.
options.C: Because its particles are tightly packed and cannot move.
options.D: Because it always remains in a solid state.

mcqs.answer: Because its particles are far apart and move freely in all directions.
mcqs.explanation: The ability of gases to flow arises from the large spaces between particles, allowing them to slide past each other easily. The other options describe properties of solids or liquids, not gases.

mcqs.question: Which statement best compares the compressibility of gases with that of liquids?

options.A: Gases are much more compressible than liquids.
options.B: Liquids are more compressible than gases.
options.C: Both gases and liquids are equally compressible.
options.D: Neither gases nor liquids can be compressed.

mcqs.answer: Gases are much more compressible than liquids.
mcqs.explanation: Because the particles in a gas are far apart, applying pressure reduces the volume significantly. In liquids, particles are already close together, so volume changes only slightly under pressure. Hence gases are far more compressible.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT a gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP)?
mcqs.explanation: At STP, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and water vapor exist as gases. Liquid water is a liquid, not a gas, making option D the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a property of gases?

options.A: Gases have no fixed shape; they take the shape of their container.
options.B: Gases retain the shape of the container in which they were first placed.
options.C: Gases have a permanent shape regardless of the container.
options.D: Gases can only exist in one shape.

mcqs.answer: Gases have no fixed shape; they take the shape of their container.
mcqs.explanation: Gases do not possess a fixed shape; they spread out to fill any container. Options B, C, and D incorrectly attribute a fixed shape to gases.

mcqs.question: What is true about the volume of a gas at a given temperature and pressure?

options.A: A gas has no fixed volume; it expands to fill the entire container.
options.B: A gas always occupies a fixed volume regardless of the container size.
options.C: A gas only expands when heated, otherwise its volume stays constant.
options.D: A gas contracts to a fixed volume when cooled.

mcqs.answer: A gas has no fixed volume; it expands to fill the entire container.
mcqs.explanation: Gases lack a fixed volume and will occupy all the space available to them. Options B, C, and D describe behaviors that are not characteristic of gases under constant conditions.

mcqs.question: How would you correctly define the ability of gases to fill available space, distinguishing it from liquids?

options.A: Gases spread out to occupy every part of the container, while liquids take the shape of the container but do not necessarily fill it completely.
options.B: Both gases and liquids always fill the entire container they are placed in.
options.C: Liquids fill all available space, whereas gases only occupy a portion of the container.
options.D: Gases remain in a fixed region of the container, unlike liquids which spread out.

mcqs.answer: Gases spread out to occupy every part of the container, while liquids take the shape of the container but do not necessarily fill it completely.
mcqs.explanation: Gases have enough kinetic energy and space between particles to expand and fill any container completely. Liquids, while taking the shape of the container, have a definite volume and therefore may not fill the entire space if the container is larger than the liquid volume.

mcqs.question: Which everyday example best illustrates the ability of a gas to flow?

options.A: Air moving through a ventilation duct.

mcqs.answer: Air moving through a ventilation duct.
mcqs.explanation: Air, a gas, moves easily through ducts, showing its ability to flow. Water (liquid), sand (granular solid), and a metal rod (solid) do not demonstrate gas flow.
